confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from two web searches. Aggregated cost-of-living data (Expatica, using Numbeo data from June 2026) gave an inexpensive meal at about EUR 19, a three-course meal for two at about EUR 52, a cappuccino at about EUR 2.1 and a 0.5 L draught beer at about EUR 3.1. Expatistan put the beer at about EUR 4, based on only a few price points. I converted at about 1.10 USD per EUR, based on the RBA cross rates from the same search. I raised the mid-range meal above the EUR 52 crowd-sourced figure because San Sebastian's restaurants are known to be expensive and July is peak season. The beer anchor is for a 0.5 L glass. I found no direct cocktail or wine data. The cocktail is estimated from Basque Country bar prices and its relationship to beer. The wine glass reflects cheap local wine (txakoli or crianza) served by the glass. Accommodation anchors are general-knowledge estimates only, with no searches or listings checked. They assume July peak-season demand, which is very high in this small coastal city, so they are the least certain anchors and could vary by 30% or more.
comparable_city_reasoning: Food prices are based on San Sebastian cost-of-living data, which puts the city about 17% above Spain's national average. Accommodation is reasoned from peak-summer prices in Bilbao, Barcelona and Biarritz, adjusted for San Sebastian's limited supply and July demand.
